findings.description: Invite codes are bearer secrets that grant workspace membership, but they are generated with `random.choices`, which uses the Mersenne Twister. Its output is predictable once enough outputs are observed, so an attacker who sees a few codes could predict others and join workspaces uninvited.
findings.suggestion: Use the `secrets` module, e.g. `"".join(secrets.choice(CODE_ALPHABET) for _ in range(CODE_LENGTH))`, or `secrets.token_urlsafe`.
findings.title: Invite codes generated with non-cryptographic PRNG

findings.description: `accept` checks only `revoked` and `uses >= max_uses`. It ignores `expires_at`, which `is_active` does check. An expired link can therefore still be used to join a workspace, making the TTL meaningless.
findings.title: accept() does not check link expiry

findings.description: `accept` creates the member and only then increments `link.uses`. The check and the increment are not atomic, so concurrent accepts of a single-use link can both pass the check and exceed `max_uses`. Separately, `accept` never checks that the link's creator is still a manager, so a link created by a since-demoted admin remains valid.
findings.suggestion: Guard check, add and increment with a lock, or increment before the add and roll back on failure. Optionally re-verify the creator's manager status.
findings.title: Invite role is not re-validated and uses are consumed non-atomically
